analysis: What changed versus the 6am brief: (1) The Amazon-Decart story is now the day's top megacap item and it threads the AI-capex theme: Amazon reportedly paying ~$7B for a Nvidia-backed chip-portability startup while Nvidia itself is in talks to buy/invest in open-weight model shop Reflection AI and the still-unconfirmed $40B SpaceX/Apollo GPU financing floats in the background - the AI supply chain is consolidating through big-ticket deals even as memory slides on Chinese competition (CXMT) and a US ITC probe into AI server power supplies. (2) META's relief bounce extended on the first hard Muse engagement data (7-day retention >30%, approaching ChatGPT) - but the dataset is one VC's X post citing Sensor Tower, so treat the move as fragile; the HN security-skeptic thread (391 pts, Oct 6) is the counterweight the price isn't discounting. (3) NVDA weakened technically: fourth straight down session plus ICAP's 'big, bearish, rising wedge' warning, while Street targets cluster at $600 for MSFT - rotation within the Mag7, not flight from it. (4) Goldman's breadth data says the index is carrying dead weight: median stock 16% below its high, 57% in a bear market, S&P +2% over the past month vs equal-weight -0.6% - a narrow tape heading into bank earnings and CPI. (5) The 'energy ceasefire' premium is back on after Brent round-tripped $102 to $106.70; the Iran-Saudi diplomatic channel is still the one genuinely new thread. Signal: bank earnings Tuesday, CPI Wednesday, ASML/TSMC midweek, FedEx after today's close. Noise: conflicting auto-aggregator % prints (S&P +0.1% vs Finnhub -0.07%), recycled stories, and the unconfirmed items (SpaceX $40B, Reflection AI, Gemini 4 Carbon, iPhone 18 Pro cuts).

community_signals.takeaway: The community's dominant Muse thread is a security/privacy critique (391 pts), a direct counterweight to today's retention-data bounce: even strong engagement numbers have to clear the trust problem before the monetization narrative (Wells Fargo's $1,000 target math) holds.

headlines.headline: Amazon in talks to buy Israeli AI startup Decart for ~$7B (WSJ, Sunday): Decart's software ports AI workloads across chip architectures (Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium); Nvidia is an investor in Decart; Anthropic walked away from a $6B deal in September after due diligence; AMZN ticked higher at the bell (+0.2% early)
headlines.why_it_matters: vertical AI-stack consolidation - another multi-billion capex-adjacent commitment as the Street debates circular AI spending; talks could still fall through or draw a rival bid (Decart has seen two suitors walk this year)

headlines.headline: NVDA -0.9% to ~$227.30 in early trading, threatening a fourth straight down session; ICAP technical strategist Walter Zimmerman warns the 18-month weekly chart is a 'big, bearish, rising wedge' - first warning signal is a decisive monthly close below $204.84, 'real problems' below $185.94
headlines.why_it_matters: the tape's AI bellwether is sliding into ASML/TSMC earnings week on weakening technicals - order-book and capex-guidance reads midweek decide whether this is rotation or a real top

headlines.headline: FT (Saturday) reports Nvidia is in talks to buy or invest more in open-weight model developer Reflection AI; Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment
